source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What is required for hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more?
choice_a: ABS is required only if built before 1990
choice_b: ABS is never required for hydraulically braked vehicles
choice_c: ABS is required if built on or after March 1, 1999
choice_d: ABS is optional regardless of build date
explanation: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999 are required to have ABS.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What indicator appears on the instrument panel of a school bus equipped with ABS?
choice_a: A green "ABS Ready" light
choice_b: A red "Brake Failure" light only
choice_c: There is no dashboard indicator for ABS
choice_d: A yellow ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: A school bus equipped with ABS will have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What happens to a vehicle's steering control when the steering wheels lock up during hard braking without ABS?
choice_a: The driver loses steering control
choice_b: Steering control is unaffected
choice_c: Steering becomes easier and more responsive
choice_d: The vehicle automatically corrects itself
explanation: When braking hard on slippery surfaces without ABS, if the steering wheels lock up, the driver loses steering control.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.2 How ABS Helps You

question: What does ABS primarily help a driver do?
choice_a: Always stop in a shorter distance than without ABS
choice_b: Avoid wheel lock up and maintain control
choice_c: Drive faster in all conditions
choice_d: Eliminate the need for regular brake maintenance
explanation: ABS helps the driver avoid wheel lock up and maintain control; the driver may or may not stop faster, but should be able to steer around an obstacle while braking.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.2 How ABS Helps You

question: In emergency braking on a bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver NOT do?
choice_a: Apply steady pressure to the brake pedal
choice_b: Steer around an obstacle while braking
choice_c: Pump the brakes
choice_d: Monitor the bus and back off the brakes if safe
explanation: In emergency braking, the driver should not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

question: How should a driver brake overall when driving a vehicle equipped with ABS?
choice_a: Slam on the brakes at every stop to test the system
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly at all times
choice_c: Avoid using the brakes and rely only on engine braking
choice_d: Brake the same way as they always have, using only the force necessary to stop safely and stay in control
explanation: When driving a vehicle with ABS, the driver should brake as they always have, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the start-up bulb check, or comes on while the bus is under way, what does this suggest?
choice_a: The driver may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels
choice_b: The bus has no brakes at all
choice_c: The engine has overheated
choice_d: The bus is exceeding its speed limit
explanation: If the lamp stays on after the bulb check, or goes on once under way, the driver may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.4 Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: If the ABS malfunctions, does the driver still have brakes?
choice_a: No, the entire braking system fails completely
choice_b: Yes, the driver still has regular brakes and should drive normally but get the system serviced soon
choice_c: Only the parking brake still works
choice_d: Only the emergency brake works, and it must be used exclusively
explanation: If the ABS malfunctions, the driver still has regular brakes; the driver should drive normally but get the system serviced soon.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.4 Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: Does ABS allow a driver to follow other vehicles more closely or drive less carefully?
choice_a: Yes, ABS is designed specifically to allow closer following distances
choice_b: Yes, but only on wet roads
choice_c: No, ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully
choice_d: Yes, ABS eliminates the need for careful driving entirely
explanation: The manual's safety reminders state ABS won't allow the driver to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: Does ABS prevent skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn?
choice_a: Yes, ABS prevents all types of skids in every situation
choice_b: Yes, but only at highway speeds
choice_c: ABS has no effect on skidding whatsoever
choice_d: No, ABS should prevent brake-induced skids but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
explanation: ABS won't prevent power or turning skids; it should prevent brake-induced skids but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: According to the manual's safety reminders, what remains the best vehicle safety feature?
choice_a: A safe driver
choice_b: The ABS system itself
choice_c: The parking brake
choice_d: The strobe lights
explanation: The manual reminds drivers that the best vehicle safety feature is still a safe driver.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: When should the overhead white strobe light on a school bus, if equipped, be used?
choice_a: Only during routine daytime operation
choice_b: When the driver has limited visibility
choice_c: Only when picking up students at school
choice_d: Continuously at all times regardless of conditions
explanation: If the bus is equipped with a roof-mounted white strobe light, it should be used when the driver has limited visibility, meaning the driver cannot easily see around the bus.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.1 Strobe Lights

question: What governs the use of strobe lights on a school bus in all instances?
choice_a: The bus manufacturer's warranty terms
choice_b: Federal law alone, with no state variation
choice_c: State or local regulations concerning the use of these lights
choice_d: The individual student's preference
explanation: In all instances, the driver must understand and obey their state or local regulations concerning the use of strobe lights.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.1 Strobe Lights

question: How does the manual describe the effect of strong winds on the side of a school bus?
choice_a: Strong winds have no measurable effect on a bus
choice_b: Winds only affect the bus if traveling in reverse
choice_c: Winds only affect the front bumper area
choice_d: The side of the bus acts like a sail on a sailboat
explanation: The manual states that the side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat, and strong winds can push the bus sideways, move it off the road, or in extreme conditions, tip it over.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.2 Driving in High Winds

question: If caught in strong winds while driving a school bus, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Keep a strong grip on the steering wheel, slow down, and consider pulling off the roadway to wait
choice_b: Speed up to get through the windy area faster
choice_c: Turn off the headlights to reduce wind resistance
choice_d: Open the windows to equalize pressure
explanation: If caught in strong winds, the driver should keep a strong grip on the steering wheel and try to anticipate gusts, slow down to lessen the effect of the wind, or pull off the roadway and wait, and contact dispatch for guidance.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.2 Driving in High Winds

question: According to the manual, when should a school bus driver back the bus?
choice_a: Whenever it is more convenient than pulling forward
choice_b: Only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle
choice_c: Backing is required at every stop
choice_d: Backing should be done frequently to practice the maneuver
explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged and should be done only when the driver has no other safe way to move the vehicle.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: Should a driver ever back a school bus when students are outside of the bus?
choice_a: Yes, as long as a lookout is posted
choice_b: Yes, but only at low speed
choice_c: No, the driver should never back a school bus when students are outside of the bus
choice_d: Yes, if the parking brake is engaged first
explanation: The manual states the driver should never back a school bus when students are outside of the bus, since backing increases the risk of a collision.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: What is the purpose of posting a lookout when backing a school bus?
choice_a: To give the driver turn-by-turn steering directions
choice_b: To operate the brakes remotely
choice_c: To count the students as they board
choice_d: To warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, not to give directions on how to back the bus
explanation: The purpose of the lookout is to warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles; the lookout should not give directions on how to back the bus.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: If no lookout is available and the driver must back the bus, what steps should be taken first?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, turn off the motor and take the keys, then walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear
choice_b: Immediately begin backing slowly while looking only in the mirrors
choice_c: Rev the engine to alert nearby students
choice_d: Ask a student to stand behind the bus as a guide
explanation: If no lookout is available, the driver should set the parking brake, turn off the motor and take the keys, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: Up to how many feet of tail swing can a school bus have?
choice_a: Up to ten feet
choice_b: Up to three feet
choice_c: Up to six inches
choice_d: A school bus has no tail swing
explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, and the driver needs to check mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor it.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.4 Tail Swing

question: What should a driver do to monitor tail swing during turning movements?
choice_a: Rely only on the overhead inside mirror
choice_b: There is no need to monitor tail swing on a school bus
choice_c: Check mirrors before and during any turning movements
choice_d: Ask a passenger to watch out the rear window
explanation: The driver needs to check mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor the tail swing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.4 Tail Swing

question: If backing up is unavoidable at a student pick-up point, what should the driver do regarding students?
choice_a: Have students board while the bus is backing
choice_b: Instruct students to wait behind the bus during backing
choice_c: Backing is never permitted at a pick-up point under any circumstances
choice_d: Pick up students before backing and watch for late comers at all times
explanation: If the driver must back up at a student pick-up point, they should be sure to pick up students before backing and watch for late comers at all times.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing
